title: GitHub Trending Today #30: clicky, Locker, graphify, qmd, parlor, gemma-gem, clawchief, KarpathyTalk

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub Awesome. This is GitHub Trending Today episode 30 and we are not slowing down. 35 trending open source projects on GitHub. Let's get into it.

sections.title: clicky
paragraphs: What if your AI tutor could see your screen, talk to you out loud, and physically point at things to guide you? Clickie is a little AI buddy that floats next to your cursor. It watches your screen, speaks to you, and points at elements directly on your monitor. Built by Farsza, the founder of Buildspace, and just fully open- sourced. Hook up your own API keys via Cloudflare worker and build your own desktop companion.

sections.title: Locker
paragraphs: Tired of paying for Dropbox or Google Drive? Locker is the open- source replacement. Bring your own bucket, S3, Cloudflare R2, Versel Blob, or a local hard drive. Locker sits on top of whatever storage you already have and gives you a beautiful Dropbox style file system. No self-hosting required. Plug in your bucket keys and you're done. It can even act as its own S3 bucket for other apps to write directly into.

sections.title: graphify
paragraphs: Andre Carpathy tweeted that there was room for an incredible product to make sense of messy local file dumps. Someone stayed up and built it. 7,000 GitHub stars in 48 hours. Graphy is a clawed code skill that compiles your entire project into a persistent graph knowledge base. a pass over your code, AI vision for diagrams and screenshots, all wired into a queryable knowledge graph. sections.title: qmd
paragraphs: AI agents. Of course, he did. QMD is a local CLI search engine built specifically for markdown files, meeting notes, and agent session histories. BM25 full text search, local vector semantic search, and an LLM reranker, all running on your hardware via Node Lama CPP. Built-in MCP support, so your agent can query hundreds of past chats without burning a single API token. Open AAI's

sections.title: parlor
paragraphs: real-time voice and vision mode is impressive. Parlor gives you the same experience running 100% locally on your MacBook. Open- source real-time multimodal AI. Live audio and webcam input talks back natively. Powered by Gemma 4 E2B for speech and vision. Cooro for texttospech running on Apple silicon via MLX. End to end latency of 2.5 to 3 seconds. You can interrupt it mid-sentence.

sections.title: mini-coding-agent
paragraphs: You use clawed code every day. But do you actually know how it works? Mini coding agent is a minimal Python implementation that demystifies the agentic harness, the software layer that gives a raw LLM tool calling, file editing, and memory. No enterprise complexity, just clean code showing exactly how an agent observes your environment, inspects a codebase, and runs a shell command.

sections.title: gemma-gem
paragraphs: What if your browser had a fully local AI that could read, click, and interact with any web page without sending a single bite to the cloud? Gemma Gem is a Chrome extension that runs Google's Gemma 4 entirely on device via WebGPU. No API keys, no subscriptions. It injects a chat overlay into any page and gives the model real tools, reading content, taking screenshots, executing JavaScript.

sections.title: clawchief
paragraphs: Claw Chief turns Open Claw into a full-time chief of staff. Every 15 minutes, it checks your email and surfaces only what actually matters. It reads Calendarly links, schedules meetings, updates your CRM in Google Sheets, does its own business development research, and manages your task list without duplicating entries. Filebased OS built around heartbeat.md and skill.md configs runs continuously on your own hardware.

sections.title: KarpathyTalk
paragraphs: Andre Karpathy got curious how fast you could build a social network with Frontier AI tools. The answer, two hours on a Sunday. Carpathy Talk is an open source developer community. Twitter meets GitHub gists built as a single go binary with SQLite and HTMX. Every post is a raw markdown document with public JSON and markdown endpoints explicitly designed for AI agents to read and scrape freely.

sections.title: badclaude
paragraphs: Bad Claude is a physics-based whip that overlays your terminal. When Claude is thinking too slowly, you click to physically whip it. It cracks, plays a sound effect, fires an interrupt, and sends a message like, "Speed it up, Clanker." The GitHub Road includes milestones like, "Get a cease and desist from Anthropic." And keep logs of who whipped Claude, so when the robots come, we can order people nicely for them.

sections.title: rtk
paragraphs: Claude code, cursor, they all burn through context fast. every git status, every npm test, dumping thousands of tokens of noisy logs straight into your LLM's memory. RTK fixes that. A Rust CLI proxy that sits between your terminal and your agent, intercepts command output, and aggressively compresses it, strips whites space, dduplicates errors, summarizes directory trees, 60 to 90% fewer tokens on common dev commands.

sections.title: CodeIsland
paragraphs: Running multiple clawed code agents across a dozen terminal tabs is chaos. You lose track of what's running, miss permission prompts, and spend half your time alt tabbing. Code Island fixes that by turning your Mac dynamic island into a real-time AI control center. See which agents are thinking or waiting for approval, track live API usage, review inline diffs, and one-click jump to the exact terminal window you need. Most

sections.title: Falcon-Perception
paragraphs: vision models use a separate encoder for images and a decoder for text. Falcon Perception ditches that entirely. It's a 6 billion parameter early fusion transformer that processes image patches and text tokens simultaneously in a single shared space. Give it an image and a natural language query. Get back pixel accurate bounding boxes, instant segmentation masks, and full OCR text.

sections.title: clauditor
paragraphs: Claude code resends your entire conversation history on every turn. A 200 turn session costs 10 times more quota than it should. Claude Eater runs in the background as a token firewall. It monitors your session's waste factor and when context bloats too far, it blocks Claude, saves your progress locally and tells you to start fresh. Open a new tab, type continue, pick up exactly where you left off.

sections.title: buddy-reroll
paragraphs: Anthropic dropped a Tamagotchi style pet system in clawed code. Your species, rarity, hat, and shiny status are locked to your user ID forever. No rolls. Buddy Roll fixes that. Select exactly what you want. Legendary shiny dragon with a top hat and it burns through millions of hashes across all your CPU cores using the bun runtime to find the perfect salt. Then patches the binary automatically.

sections.title: OpenMontage
paragraphs: Give it a topic, get back a finished video. Open Montage is the first open- source agentic video production system. It researches your idea via live web search, writes a timestamp script, generates images, video, voice narration, and background music, then stitches everything together with word level subtitles, 11 production pipelines, 49 media tools, 400 plus agent skills.

sections.title: gnhf
paragraphs: What if you just went to sleep and let your AI agents work through the night? G&HF good night have fun is a dead simple orchestrator that wraps clawed codeex open code and robo. Give it a measurable goal before bed. It runs a continuous autonomous loop all night, keeps the wins, discards the failures, and keeps going. Wake up to a solved feature or an optimized code base. What if your AI coding assistant could actually prove its math is correct?

sections.title: mathcode
paragraphs: Mathcode is a terminal-based AI assistant with a built-in math formalization engine. Give it a problem in plain English. It translates it into a rigorous lean for the writes and verifies a formal proof. No hallucinated logic. No handwaving. Compile time mathematical certainty.

sections.title: ghost-pepper
paragraphs: Hold control. Say what you want. Let go. It types it for you. Ghost pepper is a local holdto talk speechtoext app for Apple silicon. No cloud APIs, no audio leaving your machine, zero latency waiting on a server. The filler word cleanup is what made it blow up on hacker news. You speak naturally. It pastes clean text, dictate code, write emails, talk to your local AI agents without touching the keyboard.

sections.title: GuppyLM
paragraphs: Guppy LM is a 9 million parameter language model built from scratch that does exactly one thing. Pretends to be a small fish named Guppy. No swigloo, no rope, just a pure vanilla sixlayer transformer. trains in five minutes on a free Collab T4 GPU. The entire pipeline is exposed. Data generation, BP tokenizer, training, architecture, training loop, inference. Ask it the meaning of life. It says food. The answer is always food.

sections.title: tailslayer
paragraphs: DRAM memory refresh stalls have caused unpredictable latency spikes since the 1960s. Nobody fixed it. Lori Wire just did. Tail Slayer is a C++ library that replicates your data across multiple physical DRAM channels, exploiting undocumented memory channel scrambling offsets, so refresh schedules become completely uncorrelated. Then it races both channels against each other in a hedged read. Whichever isn't refreshing wins.

sections.title: macpow
paragraphs: Ever wonder exactly what's draining your MacBook battery? Macpow is a real-time power tree TUI written in Rust that reads directly from IO report and the SMC collapsible hierarchy of your entire systems power consumption per core CPU and GPU utilization temperatures RAM network traffic and energy drain attributed down to individual processes no pseudo required works from M1 all the way to M5.

sections.title: sage-wiki
paragraphs: Keeping a personal wiki updated is a chore nobody actually does. Sage Wiki makes your AI the maintainer instead. Drop raw PDFs or web clippings into a folder and the AI autonomously creates summary pages, links concepts, resolves contradictions, and runs health checks on your knowledge graph. The mental model, Obsidian is the IDE. Your AI is the programmer. Your wiki is the codebase.

sections.title: fieldtheory-cli
paragraphs: Your Xbookmarks are a black hole. You save threads, never find them again. Field theory CLI pulls your entire X archive to your local machine and dumps it into a SQLite database with full text search. One terminal command. Find that system design thread from 6 months ago in seconds. Built-in LLM classification autotags your content. Pipe JSON output straight into Obsidian or a local rag pipeline.

sections.title: three-man-team
paragraphs: Solo AI coding sessions get chaotic fast. Your agent burns tokens, reads half your code base, and hallucinates features nobody asked for. Threeman team fixes that by splitting your LLM into three personas. An architect that scopes your request into a tight brief. A builder that writes only what's in the brief. A reviewer that ruthlessly rejects anything that doesn't match the spec.

sections.title: gemma-tuner-multimodal
paragraphs: Fine-tuning a multimodal AI usually means renting expensive cloud GPUs. This project kills that requirement entirely. Gemma tuner multimodal lets you fine-tune Gemma 4 and Gemma 3N with full audio image and text support directly on Apple silicon. PyTorch with metal performance shaders under the hood. Mac Studio or a MacBook with decent unified memory is all you need.

sections.title: storm
paragraphs: Traditional terminal UI frameworks repaint every cell on every state change. Write one character and it redraws all 10,000 cells. Storm fixes that by treating your terminal like a real display server. Cell-level diff renderer using typed array buffers. Zero new JavaScript objects per frame. 90% less garbage collection pressure. Skips up to 97% of the terminal on a typical frame. You let your AI agent write a bunch of code. Now you have to blindly trust it or squint through raw terminal

sections.title: revdiff
paragraphs: output to see what changed. RevDiff fixes that. Type /revd diff and it opens a syntax highlighted diff overlay inside your terminal with git blame gutters. Navigate vim style. Leave inline annotations on exact lines. Hit quit. Claude reads your plans the fixes applies them and you re-review instantly.

sections.title: textual-diff-view
paragraphs: Building a Python terminal app that needs to show code diffs. This is the widget you've been waiting for. Textual diff view is a standalone textual widget that renders syntax highlighted diffs inside your TUI. Unified or sidebyside split view. Deleted lines in red, added lines in green, plus and minus annotations for full colorblind accessibility. Full light and dark theme support out of the box.

sections.title: handoff
paragraphs: What if you could take a web RTC session from your browser and hand full control to a go process you own? Handoff by the Pyen team does exactly that. Start a call on Zoom or Google Meet normally, then transparently forward the media connection to your backend. Record the stream, inject custom video via FFmpeg, pipe an AI talking head directly into a live call, or capture and decrypt raw ICE and RTP traffic for deep reverse engineering.

sections.title: envradar
paragraphs: You clone a repo, spin up the dev server, and it immediately crashes because someone forgot to document an environment variable. Enverdar fixes that. It scans your source code across Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go, plus Docker Compose files, and GitHub actions workflows and compares everything against yourv.ample file.

sections.title: loophole
paragraphs: What if you could stress test any set of rules until they broke? Loophole is an adversarial AI system that tears apart laws, contracts, and licenses. Six specialized agents. Two exploit loopholes. Two find overreach. One judges. One patches the text after each round to make it bulletproof. The creator fed it Azimov's three laws of robotics and broke them completely in under 30 minutes for 80 cents in API costs.

sections.title: slopc
paragraphs: What if your Rust compiler just wrote the function for you? Slopsy is a procedural macro that sends your function signature and doc comment to an LLM at compile time and generates the implementation on the spot. If the generated code fails to compile, it intercepts the Rust compiler errors, feeds them back to the LLM, and retries until it passes, then runs your doc test assertions to verify the logic.

sections.title: claude-skill-app-onboarding-questionnaire
paragraphs: Your onboarding flow is killing your conversions. This skill fixes that. It's a claude code skill that teaches your AI to design and build questionnaire style onboarding flows modeled on the psychological conversion patterns used by Headspace and N. Tell it what your app does. It generates the complete frictionless signup flow.

sections.title: skwd-wall
paragraphs: If you rice your Linux desktop, this one's for you. SW wall is a way wallpaper selector that supports static images, live videos, and full steam wallpaper engine scenes. Three animated presentation modes, including a parallelogram carousel and hexagon grid. Built-in Steam Workshop and Wall Haven browsers for downloading wallpapers directly inside the app.
